newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures wilt despite dollar strength.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures wilt despite dollar strength.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures ended easier on some late stop-loss sales as the market failed to sustain initial gains, dealers said on Thursday.
The benchmark Nikkei 225 December contract got off to a strong start on the back of a firm overnight close in Chicago and the dollar's strength against the yen.

But a lack of follow-through buying weighed on the market, pushing the contract down to 21,355 at the close against a previous settlement at 21,485. Dealers said stop-loss sales were triggered at 21,360, taking it to a low of 21,310.
"There was some early buying but it stopped. And locals pushed the market down looking for stop orders so they could cover their shorts," said a dealer with a European institution.
He said about 500 futures went through at the 21,360 level but that was enough to move the market as total turnover was only 11,515 lots.

He said the dollar's bullish tone was likely to filter through to Nikkei cash and futures markets soon, but added, "I'm not overly bullish. I think it (December Nikkei)'s going to hit its head on 21,800 and come off."
